summary: Part 1 of 3 of the Revibe training video "6.0 Returns (Seller)" (00:00 to 06:38), checked against all 40 frames in the pack (t00000 to t00397). The trainer explains the return-claim rules and the Revibe Return Process slide, then shows a customer raising a claim on the customer account page, then the seller side in the admin portal (Claim Management > R - Seller Returns): opening claim o941bQ, reviewing its sections, and the Mark valid / Mark invalid buttons. Several frames show customer personal data and the presenter's personal file names. Some spoken words are unreliable (the trainer's '{rational?}' and 'above 95 {%?}' are not confirmed). The slide footer labels Ship-Back as 'sent to customer', which does not match the valid-lab outcome where the device goes back to the seller.

terms.meaning: A customer request to return a device, raised on the customer account portal. Shown with a claim ID such as o941bQ, a claim type (Issue) and a request (Return).
15 days from delivery in which a customer can return a device.
A further valid claim on the same order; accepted even after the 15-day period.
Step 2: the Revibe team checks the customer's proof; if validated, the request is marked Completed.
The airway bill for the pickup. Auto-created for AE & ZA orders (trainer: UAE and South Africa); created manually by the seller for SA orders (trainer: Saudi Arabia).
Order-country codes on the slide. AE & ZA = auto AWB; SA = seller creates the AWB manually. The trainer names the countries as UAE and South Africa (AE & ZA) and Saudi Arabia (SA).
Claim stages before the device reaches the seller; AE & ZA claims move to Under Collection immediately after the AWB is created.
Stage in which the device has reached the seller and the seller chooses Mark valid or Mark invalid.
The two seller decisions on a claim; valid triggers an immediate refund and closure, invalid requires proof.

unclear.issue: Word 'rational' (transcript '{rational?}') is unreliable. The slide shows 'Required: written message + supporting proof' (t00140.jpg), but the spoken word is not confirmed. Do not state the exact proof wording from the audio alone.

'above 95 {%?} for instance' is the trainer's example, not a stated rule. The threshold and the % sign are unconfirmed, and no threshold appears on screen (the customer help text only asks for a screenshot showing the % of Battery Health, t00242.jpg). Do not present 95% as a requirement.

Ship-back label conflict. The slide and the trainer agree that in the Revibe Lab valid case the device goes back to the seller ('Valid → full refund + ship back to seller', t00180.jpg; 'device will be shipped back to you'). The slide footer, however, labels Ship-Back as 'Ship-Back (sent to customer)' (t00000.jpg), and the portal side panel calls the block 'Shipback Tracking Information' (t00340.jpg). Which party the Ship-Back tracking block refers to is unclear.

Trainer says a pop-up window will appear for the invalid proof. No such pop-up is shown in any frame of this part. The seller screens show the Attachments area and upload dialog (t00366.jpg, t00397.jpg). Where the written message is entered on the seller side is not shown.

Claim Management has several seller return menus: R - Revibe Returns, R - Seller Returns, R - Seller Request and R - Seller Returns SA (t00288.jpg). The trainer only says 'seller returns' and does not explain the differences. Which one applies to a given case is unclear.

Explanation to show text is cut off on screen: 'We received your device and we are running our investigation process. This process will take from 2 to 4 day' (t00325.jpg). The full duration wording is not visible.

Statuses fields such as 'Refund to cx status', 'Refund to supplier status' and 'Valid claim' are shown, but the trainer does not explain what sets them or who fills them. 'Customer paid?' is in the Claim Details section, not Statuses, and is also not explained. Their purpose is unclear.
